question: Why do certain people fail to know the supreme truth according to the ladle analogy?
premises: The supreme truth is not known by them
A ladle in cooking does not taste the juice
An analogy illustrates indirect contact without realization
inference: They do not know the supreme truth, just as a ladle does not know the taste of the cooking.
uncertainties: The subject of jānanti is implied from context as those lacking true understanding.
plain_english: They do not know the supreme truth, just as a ladle does not know the taste of what it cooks.
